origin_classes.P: population prior (literature value, not measured on this dataset)
origin_classes.F: fitted (fitted_to states what it was fitted to)

connectome.sugar_knn.fitted_to: leave-one-out classification of the left LB3 neurons (Shiu sugar vs other) on FlyWire v783; k=5 gave 19/20 sugar, 2/44 false positives (Synaptera v1 selection, anatomy only)

connectome.nt_modulatory.source: dopamine, serotonin and octopamine act as slow neuromodulators; the Shiu model nevertheless treats them as fast excitation. Classification from the Synaptera v1 --nt-modulatory-silent decision (SPEC_BRAIN_CONTROL Step 0 decisions II); used only by the named model variant 'silent'

connectome.pred_sign_shiu.source: Shiu et al. 2023 model rule: every transmitter other than GABA / glutamate is excitatory; used by the 'impute' variant to give a predicted neuron its vote. HIST and TYR (BANC) have no entry on purpose: F1 decision

connectome.fast_nt_sign.source: Shiu et al. 2023 sign mapping for the three fast transmitters (ACh excitatory; GABA, glutamate inhibitory); applied to the literature transmitter of Schlegel et al. 2024 known_nt by the 'literature' variant

engine.shiu.v_0.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); resting potential, Kakaria & de Bivort 2017

engine.shiu.v_rst.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); reset potential, Kakaria & de Bivort 2017

engine.shiu.v_th.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); spike threshold, Kakaria & de Bivort 2017

engine.shiu.t_mbr.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); membrane time constant, Kakaria & de Bivort 2017

engine.shiu.tau.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); synaptic time constant, Juergensen et al. 2021

engine.shiu.t_rfc.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); refractory period, Lazar et al. 2021

engine.shiu.t_dly.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); synaptic delay, Paul et al. 2015

engine.shiu.w_syn.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); weight per synapse; Shiu et al. describe it as the model's one free parameter
engine.shiu.w_syn.fitted_to: UNVERIFIED: the quantity w_syn was fitted to is not stated in this repository; fill from Shiu et al. 2023 before any claim that rests on it

engine.shiu.f_poi.source: philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model@91bdd1e model.py default_params (read at run time from the pinned, hashed file); scaling of the Poisson synapse; model.py comment: '250 is sufficient to cause spiking'

engine.clock_dt_ms.source: Brian2 default clock the Shiu model was run at; engine asserts advance() is a multiple of it

engine.history_ms.source: length of the recent-spike window kept for rates(); a larger rates() window raises

connectome.dev_min_syn.source: synaptera@c94796d:flight/brain.py DEV_MIN_SYN; partner threshold of the DEV subnet (never a result)

coupling.interval_ms.source: docs/05_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md 3.4: 25 ms is too coarse for reflexes; the scheduler reads it from the configuration, the engine takes whatever advance(dt_ms) it is given
